summary.headline: Windlas Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% Y-o-Y to a record INR248 crores, with CDMO up 29% and Trade Generics hit by codeine discontinuation.
summary.overview: Revenue hit a record INR248 crores, up 18% Y-o-Y, extending the company's record-revenue run to 14 consecutive quarters. Adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) rose 26% Y-o-Y to INR34 crores, with PAT of INR25 crores up 37%. The Generic Formulations CDMO vertical grew 29% to INR207 crores, while Trade Generics & Institutional fell to INR30 crores after codeine-based products were discontinued. Management said Plant 6 is expected to be fully online at end-H1 FY27, targeting around INR1,100 crores of revenue capacity, and repeatedly declined to attribute the CDMO spike to any specific factor.

financial_highlights.change: lower after codeine discontinuation; Y-o-Y decline not quantified

financial_highlights.value: INR13 crores, INR6.30 per equity share

segments.name: Generic Formulations CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR207 crores, +29% Y-o-Y, driven by customer expansion, deeper engagement and new launches. Management said the quarter's growth should not be treated as a base rate and volume was the main driver, though API price benefit could not be quantified.

segments.name: Trade Generics & Institutional
segments.commentary: Revenue INR30 crores after discontinuation of codeine-based cough syrups. Management acknowledged a momentum hit and called it temporary, but did not guide on recovery timing. Analysts noted the ex-codeine base has been flat for 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue INR11 crores, +79% Y-o-Y on a small base. Management described it as a higher-gestation business and cited ongoing registrations, new geographies and plant audits.

segments.name: Injectables
segments.commentary: Not separately disclosed; now contributing to overall revenue. Management confirmed that injectables are back on track on customer feedback, inquiries and offtake.

guidance_outlook: Plant 6 (core dosage expansion) expected to be commercialised by end of H1 FY27, with a possible slip of about 15 days.
Plant 6 is expected to add about INR30 million of quarterly depreciation initially (±10-15%), with full impact from Q3 FY27.
Revenue capacity from current plants plus Plant 6 is put at about INR1,100 crores, with management seeing a further INR100-150 crores possible through debottlenecking.
Maintenance capex runs at INR12-15 crores a year. Management does not give formal guidance on growth.
capex_capacity: Plant 6 mechanical completion is done; validations and customer audits are ongoing, with commercialisation targeted for end-H1 FY27.
Current utilisation is about 65%. Management says the practical peak is 60-65%, stretchable to about 70%.
Injectables already has the building and utilities set up for additional lines. A new injectables capacity decision would take about 6-8 months to add and qualify machinery.
Oral solids brownfield expansion is estimated to take about 1 year to bring online. A new dosage form would take longer.
Some machines bought for Plant 6 were used in Plant 2 and its extension this quarter, adding to revenue.
demand_pricing: Indian pharma (IPM) volume growth was 3.4% in Q1 FY27. Management said it is watching this as a welcome sign but does not see a clear trend change.

API prices remain volatile after the West Asia crisis and crude moves. Management said it is cost-plus, that customers share pricing benefits, and that it could not quantify any API price gain in the quarter.
Management said inventory and receivable days rose during the quarter because of geopolitical factors, and that working capital was back to similar levels by quarter-end.
Employee costs ex-ESOP grew about 17% Y-o-Y, which management attributed to volume-linked contract manpower, wage increases and a retrospective Uttarakhand minimum wage revision.
Gross margin improvement was attributed to business mix, operational efficiencies and higher-value CDMO products. Management said it does not manage quarterly margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 29% CDMO growth sustainable, and is injectables adding to it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly growth should not be read as a base, and that injectables have been contributing for some time without a specific quarter-driving factor. Long-term drivers have not changed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company close the gap in Trade Generics after codeine is removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more SKUs (150-200 in the range, with much room to grow), new state and geographic openings, and better execution. It declined to give a growth outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak utilisation, and can revenue go beyond INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,100 crores is a base level. Efficiency initiatives could add 10-15%, and INR100-150 crores more is possible with Plant 6, while peak utilisation is 60-65%, stretchable to about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 17% ex-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited volume-driven contract manpower, annual increments and a retrospective Uttarakhand minimum wage increase notified about 2-3 months earlier. It said nothing was extraordinary.

qa_highlights.question: Has the API price environment changed the top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not quantify the benefit. Some customers passed through price increases on existing orders, and the volatility has not settled.

qa_highlights.question: How long from planning to revenue for the next expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a brownfield oral solids expansion takes about 1 year, a new dosage form takes longer, and it favours incremental capacity over large blocks.

risks_watch: Trade Generics & Institutional has been flat for 3-4 quarters after codeine removal, and management gave no recovery timeline.
Plant 6 commercialisation at end-H1 FY27, plus customer plant-level approvals, which will determine the revenue ramp and depreciation step-up.
Quarterly CDMO growth may have been lifted by API price pass-through and one-off conversions. Management could not split volume from price.
Rising ex-ESOP employee costs (about +17%) and higher working capital (inventory and receivable days) could pressure margins.
Exports remain small (INR11 crores) and lumpy, and dossier wins are not disclosed.
